"such as" already implies you're listing a few examples so "and so on" is not necessary.

Bit of a nitpick, but if the reader is absolutely interested in `seek_end` they can check it on their own. This line seems be about what the file cursor is and how to control it, not to go in-depth about each method, which would otherwise ruin the flow. So:
```suggestion
		A [FileAccess] instance has its own file cursor, which is the position in bytes in the file where the next read/write operation will occur. Functions such as [method get_8], [method get_16], [method store_8], and [method store_16] will move the file cursor forward by the number of bytes read/written. The file cursor can be moved to a specific position using [method seek] or [method seek_end]. The current position of the file cursor can be retrieved using [method get_position].
```
or
```suggestion
		A [FileAccess] instance has its own file cursor, which is the position in bytes in the file where the next read/write operation will occur. Functions such as [method get_8], [method get_16], [method store_8], and [method store_16] will move the file cursor forward by the number of bytes read/written. The file cursor can be moved to a specific position using [method seek] or [method seek_end], and its position can be retrieved using [method get_position].
```
